question: Even if species do not share the same global transition geography, is flower-colour composition itself spatially structured within species?

primary_species_frame.rationale: Reuse the previously established reliable within-species frame from the H4 capacity audit; this threshold is not selected from H6 outcomes.

spatial_unit.aggregation: species x frozen 18x9 equal-area H1 cell
spatial_unit.cell_colour: mean soft four-group composition collapsed from the retained nine flower palette fractions and renormalized to unit mass
spatial_unit.pairwise_geographic_distance: great-circle kilometres between H1 cell centroids
spatial_unit.pairwise_colour_distance: Jensen-Shannon divergence in bits between species-cell soft colour compositions

primary_statistic.species_level: Spearman correlation between pairwise geographic distance and pairwise colour JSD
primary_statistic.global: equal-species mean of evaluable species-level Spearman correlations

null.operation: independently permute species-cell colour labels within each species while preserving occupied geography, cell support, colour compositions, and species identity

decision_rule.support: primary evaluable species >=30, observed equal-species mean rho > 0, and one-sided permutation p_upper < 0.05
decision_rule.otherwise: no support for general species-specific spatial structuring

claim_ceiling: A supported H6 would show that flower-colour composition tends to diverge with geographic separation within species across the exploratory multi-species photo frame. It would not show that different species share the same boundary, identify a climate driver, establish adaptation or selection, or establish pigment or pollinator mechanism.
